canonical_statement: The EMPA-REG OUTCOME trial evaluated empagliflozin versus placebo for cardiovascular morbidity and mortality in adults with type 2 diabetes at high cardiovascular risk receiving standard care.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: we examined the effects of empagliflozin, as compared with placebo

canonical_statement: EMPA-REG OUTCOME was a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled cardiovascular outcomes trial conducted at 590 sites in 42 countries.
The event-driven trial continued until at least 691 adjudicated primary outcome events had occurred.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: until an adjudicated primary outcome event had occurred in at least 691 patients

canonical_statement: Eligible participants were adults with type 2 diabetes, body-mass index no greater than 45, and eGFR at least 30 mL/min/1.73 m².
All enrolled patients were required to have established cardiovascular disease as defined by protocol cardiovascular-risk criteria.

population.label: Adults with type 2 diabetes and established cardiovascular disease

canonical_statement: Drug-naive participants required HbA1c 7.0% to 9.0%, whereas participants on stable glucose-lowering therapy required HbA1c 7.0% to 10.0%.

population.label: Glycemic eligibility population
inclusion_criteria: HbA1c 7.0%-9.0% if no glucose-lowering agent for >=12 weeks
HbA1c 7.0%-10.0% if stable glucose-lowering therapy for >=12 weeks

canonical_statement: After a 2-week open-label placebo run-in, participants were randomized 1:1:1 to empagliflozin 10 mg once daily, empagliflozin 25 mg once daily, or placebo.
One intervention arm received empagliflozin 10 mg orally once daily.
One intervention arm received empagliflozin 25 mg orally once daily.
The control arm received matching placebo once daily against background standard care.
Randomization was stratified by screening HbA1c, baseline BMI, screening eGFR category, and geographic region.

Background glucose-lowering therapy was intended to remain unchanged for the first 12 weeks unless rescue intensification was needed; after week 12 investigators could adjust therapy to local glycemic targets.
Investigators were encouraged throughout follow-up to manage dyslipidemia, hypertension, and other cardiovascular risk factors according to local standards of care.
The primary outcome was time to cardiovascular death, nonfatal myocardial infarction excluding silent myocardial infarction, or nonfatal stroke (3-point MACE).

outcome.definition: Cardiovascular death, nonfatal myocardial infarction excluding silent myocardial infarction, or nonfatal stroke

canonical_statement: The key secondary outcome added hospitalization for unstable angina to the 3-point MACE components (4-point MACE).

outcome.definition: 3-point MACE plus hospitalization for unstable angina

canonical_statement: Safety events were assessed during treatment or within 7 days after the last dose and coded using MedDRA version 18.0.

outcome.definition: Adverse events during treatment or within 7 days after last dose

canonical_statement: Confirmed hypoglycemia was defined as plasma glucose less than 70 mg/dL or an event requiring assistance.

outcome.definition: Plasma glucose <70 mg/dL (3.9 mmol/L) or an event requiring assistance

canonical_statement: Complicated urinary tract infection was defined as pyelonephritis, urosepsis, or a serious adverse event consistent with urinary tract infection.

outcome.definition: Pyelonephritis, urosepsis, or serious adverse event consistent with urinary tract infection

canonical_statement: The prespecified four-step hierarchy tested pooled empagliflozin versus placebo for noninferiority on 3-point MACE, noninferiority on 4-point MACE, superiority on 3-point MACE, and superiority on 4-point MACE.
The final primary noninferiority margin was a hazard ratio of 1.3; a Haybittle–Peto correction for an interim analysis yielded a final alpha of 0.0249 one-sided (0.0498 two-sided).

canonical_statement: Protocol Amendment 3 changed the cardiovascular noninferiority objective from an earlier sequential 1.8 then 1.3 margin to ruling out a hazard ratio of 1.3 or more.

canonical_statement: The primary analysis used a modified intention-to-treat treated set of randomized patients who received at least one dose; Cox regression adjusted for treatment, age, sex, baseline BMI, HbA1c, eGFR, and region.
Cumulative-incidence estimates accounted for death as a competing risk except all-cause mortality, which used Kaplan–Meier estimates.
An independent University of Freiburg analysis of cardiovascular outcomes supplemented sponsor-conducted data analyses.
A total of 7,028 participants were randomized; 7,020 received at least one dose and were included in the primary analysis.
Overall, 97.0% completed the study, 25.4% prematurely discontinued study drug, and final vital status was available for 99.2%.
Premature study-drug discontinuation occurred in 29.3% of placebo recipients versus 23.4% of pooled empagliflozin recipients.

quantitative_result.effect_measure: incidence proportion in pooled empagliflozin arm

canonical_statement: At baseline, pooled empagliflozin participants had mean age 63.1 years; 71.2% were male, 72.6% White, 21.5% Asian, and 5.1% Black/African-American.

Established cardiovascular disease was extensive at baseline: coronary artery disease 75.6%, prior myocardial infarction 46.7%, prior stroke 23.1%, peripheral artery disease 21.0%, and cardiac failure 9.9% in pooled empagliflozin participants.
Mean baseline HbA1c was 8.07% and 57.0% of pooled empagliflozin participants had type 2 diabetes for more than 10 years.
Baseline glucose-lowering therapy in the pooled empagliflozin group included metformin in 73.8%, insulin in 48.0%, sulfonylureas in 43.0%, DPP-4 inhibitors in 11.3%, and GLP-1 agonists in 2.7%.

Baseline cardiovascular preventive therapy was common: 94.9% used antihypertensive therapy, 81.0% ACE inhibitor or ARB therapy, 81.5% lipid-lowering therapy, 77.4% statins, and 82.7% acetylsalicylic acid in the pooled empagliflozin group.
Median treatment duration was 2.6 years in both pooled empagliflozin and placebo groups; median observation was 3.2 versus 3.1 years, respectively.

canonical_statement: The authors concluded that empagliflozin lowered 3-point MACE and all-cause mortality versus placebo when added to standard care in high-risk patients with type 2 diabetes.
The authors interpreted the primary composite benefit as driven by cardiovascular-death reduction, with no significant between-group reduction in myocardial infarction or stroke.
The authors reported significantly lower heart-failure hospitalization with empagliflozin and no superiority for the key 4-point MACE endpoint because unstable-angina hospitalization was similar.

The trial population consisted of patients with type 2 diabetes and established cardiovascular disease/high cardiovascular risk, so the reported number needed to treat and outcome effects cannot be extrapolated directly to populations with different clinical characteristics.
The authors estimated that 39 patients would need to be treated for 3 years to prevent one death based on the observed 32% relative reduction in all-cause mortality.

population.label: Adults with type 2 diabetes and established cardiovascular disease/high cardiovascular risk

canonical_statement: The mechanisms responsible for the early cardiovascular and mortality benefits were not established by the trial and were explicitly described by the authors as speculative and potentially multidimensional.
Subgroup interaction analyses were not adjusted for multiple testing, and cardiovascular-death subgroup analyses were post hoc.
Approximately one quarter of participants prematurely discontinued study medication, although study completion and vital-status ascertainment remained high.
The trial was supported by Boehringer Ingelheim and Eli Lilly.
Several authors reported financial relationships with manufacturers, and multiple authors were employees of Boehringer Ingelheim; disclosure forms were available with the article.
Boehringer Ingelheim participated in trial design and analyzed the data, although cardiovascular outcomes also underwent an independent statistical analysis by the University of Freiburg.
